chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, and a number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Nasr, all together, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The divorced woman, when she sees the blood of the third menstruation, has become irrevocably divorced from him.
ai.seo_question: When does a revocable divorce become irrevocable for a divorced woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of prominent Kufi scholars like Zurarah and Ja'far al-Sadiq, clarifies the transition from revocable (Raj'i) to irrevocable (Ba'in) divorce based on the completion of three menstrual cycles. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on physical signs as definitive markers for the termination of the waiting period (Iddah), ensuring legal clarity for remarriage. The ruling highlights the precision with which early Imams interpreted Quranic verses regarding divorce, linking biological reality directly to legal status.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, and a number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Nasr, both together, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
The divorced woman, when she sees the blood from her third menstruation, so she is irrevocably divorced from him’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr and A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn abu Nasr all from Jamil ibn Darraj from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
When a divorced woman experiences blood discharge of the third Hayd (menses) she becomes stranger to him.’”
